correctness.rationale: The continuous positive/negative barycentric-part retraction of two unequal graph points is graph-automorphism- and particle-swap-equivariant; difference remains ((1-u)+u/s)(α−β)≠0, and disjoint-support configurations are fixed, so it descends to the orbit quotient without a nonequivariant descent assumption. The finite deleted cubical configuration model has 28 vertices, 72 edges, 42 squares; independent reconstruction of all 142 vertices, 480 edges and 336 triangles in its barycentric subdivision and all 48 cube symmetries yielded exactly (8,15,8) orbit cells. Fresh independent quotient incidence calculation validated each of eight triangle–edge and seven edge–vertex elementary collapses at the instant applied, reducing to vertex 7; therefore X/G contractible. The proof does not confuse the Euler characteristic −2 of X with the quotient.

value.rationale: The full-symmetry quotient of graph configuration spaces is a natural moduli object and differs strongly from its nontrivial unreduced configuration space. Exact contractibility with a transparent finite Δ-complex collapse is a useful nonroutine example of a quotient changing topology, and can serve as a benchmark for equivariant graph braid computations. This specific canonical graph and full symmetry group are motivated, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
